title: Admired bassists and teachers; bowing versus picking
summary: He names bassists he admired, credits Chester Zardis with teaching him to swing, and explains that bass players mostly bowed.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Um, can you remember any of the other early bass players that you uh, liked?

Yeah, I liked it uh, I like, I can't call this fella Ellick, his name is Ellick. He's a very good bass player. His last name, I always wished to play bass like him when I grew up. And also uh, also Pop Foster, George Foster. That's another one, I always admired his bass playing. I always wished to play bass like him. And then uh, when I started playing bass, Liv Newton started me off and then I got hooked up with Chester, Chester Zardes. And I know the music some, but I didn't know very much. And Chester showed me how to uh, to swing. He showed me the swing part in the deal. Chester's the one who started me out. And uh, the voice uh, uh, Richard McClain liked me to music too. He taught me too. And also Pinchback Turo taught me. And uh, I had uh, Chester he showed me the swing in the band, how to play, learned me how to play.
In those days were you using the bow or picking?

I did more bowing than picking. Very little picking I did at that time. The uh, just on, on, on the, on the uh, beginning you'd, you'd, you'd start the bowing and maybe come out on the end you would pick a little bit.
Yeah, the last chorus you might pick some. So I could bow better than I could pick at that time. But now I can pick better.
Did most of the bass players uh, pick or bow in those days?
Bow, bow. Most all of them. All of them bowed. Very few. Um, not very much picking.
And you remember the first one you heard pick? Did Newton pick too?
Yeah, he picked but he did more bowing. Mm-hmm. This guy Ellick was a very good picker and also a bow. Mm-hmm. Mm-hmm.
